newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas firms after 20-day fall.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas firms after 20-day fall.

text.p: Gasoline prices prices finally rebounded on Tuesday after a 20-day fall on the support of a Dutch trader.
The trader bought two 50,000-barrel cargoes lifting May 7-11 of 97-octane unleaded at $24.00 per barrel and 95-octane unleaded at $23.75, from a European major.
The last gasoline fixed price trade was on March 31 for 50,000-barrels of 95-octane lifting April 15-19 at $27.00, traders said.
The Dutch trader continued to support the the market, bidding $24.30 for 97-octane, $23.85 for the 95-octane and $23.65 for the 92-octane.
On Monday, the trader bid the 95-octane unleaded grade at $23.50 per barrel fob lifting May 12-16, against a Japanese trader's offer at $23.75.
But some traders still saw the amply supplied market staying soft in the near-term.
"There is still a little bit more downward pressure," said a major. "But it is in no one's interest to depress the market unnecessarily."
The blip in Singapore prices, however, have made some traders cautious in their offers into the Taiwan tender.
A company official said Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) awarded its tender to buy leaded 95-octane reformate but will only award its unleaded tender on Wednesday.

The tender, which closed April 21 and is valid for two days, sought a 250,000-barrel cargo of unleaded reformate for delivery May 16-31 and/or June 1-15 and a 250,000-barrel cargo of leaded reformate for June 1-15 arrival.
CPC has asked traders to match the low offer for unleaded 95-octane reformate by a South Korean refiner at $24.50 per barrel c-and-f, sources said.
"The number is not so good," the official said on the unleaded offers. "We have asked the sellers to recounter their offers."
Sources said the leaded cargo was awarded to a Dutch trader at $25.20 per barrel, c-and-f to Keelung, Taichung, Kaohsiung or Shalung.

In its last tender for May 1-15 delivery, CPC bought two unleaded cargoes at $27.40 per barrel, c-and-f, from South Korean refiner Yukong and Dutch trader Vitol, and an unleaded cargo from Swiss trader Glencore at $27.70.
Naphtha firmed with crude with May and June swaps rising a hefty 65 cents per barrel to $21.45/$21.55.
